name: crossing water

attributes.attribute: offered protection from the wild hunt
often lived on islands in or under lakes

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A common folk belief kept fairies from crossing running water. People held this idea in some Celtic areas, such as the Isle of Man. If the wild hunt pursued a person, running across a stream offered protection. Standing water gave no help. Fairies in Ireland often made their homes on islands that sat in or below the wave tops of lakes.

okr.objective: Crossing running water is a folkloric protection motif.
key_results: In some Celtic lands fairies could not cross running water.
Running across a stream offered protection from the wild hunt.
Standing water gave no help to the pursued.
Fairies in Ireland were said to live on islands in or under lakes.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
